question.text: Not to be accused of lacking attention to detail, Amin also clarified that he was the conqueror of this country "in Particular". Idi Amin brutally ruled this country for most of the 1970s, during which he expelled all Asians from it.
question.clue: The issuance of the Common Man's Charter in this country was part of a socialist doctrine called the Move to the Left, which also involved taking control of sixty percent of eighty corporations after the Nakivubo Pronouncement.

swap.leadin: In a "Free State" with this name, the Force Publique terrorized workers extracting rubber.
swap.text: Give the name of that colony personally owned by Leopold II. The colony shared this name with two modern-day nations led from Kinshasa and Brazzaville.
swap.answerHtml: Congo [accept Congo Free State or Republic of the Congo or Democratic Republic of the Congo]
swap.clue: A kingdom of this name converted to Christianity under Afonso I and supplied most of the slaves sold at Sao Tome; that Portuguese kingdom of this name was located in present-day Angola.

question.text: 1493 also featured Askia Muhammad usurping Sonni Baru to become leader of this empire. He would later enact many political and religious reforms within this empire, though it wouldn't reach the extent it did under Sonni Ali.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.text: This river passes through the cities of Bamako and Timbuktu as well as the capital of its namesake country, Niamey. It enters the Gulf of Guinea.
swap.clue: In the 1990s, the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People, or MOSOP, was founded by Ken Saro-Wiwa to protest the exploitation of the oil resources of this river's delta.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Cuban involvement in African wars.
question.text: Along with the Soviet Union, Cuba supported Samora Machel and his FRELIMO party in this country's civil war. This country's opposition party RENAMO wanted the AK-47 to be removed from its flag.
question.clue: A right-wing organization opposing the socialist government of this country drew support from such cities as the Beira port in Sofala province, was formed by Andre Matsangaissa, and laid down its arms in the 1990s following the Rome Accords.

swap.text: The Evian Accords provided independence for this former French colony in North Africa.
swap.clue: This colony's 40 years of military rule ended with the redistribution of 450,000 hectares of land following the Mokrani Revolt.

question.leadin: This man envisioned a railroad stretching from the Cape to Cairo.
question.text: Name this diamond magnate and founder of the De Beers mining company. He names a scholarship to study at Oxford University in Britain.
question.clue: This man's unrealized dream was a south to north railway project called "Cape to Cairo."

swap.text: This African nation also resisted European colonization under charismatic muslim leaders like the Mahdi, but was decisively crushed at the Battle of Omdurman. Mahdist forces had also helped retake Khartoum, leading to the death of Chinese Gordon.
swap.clue: One referendum run by this country used images of clasped and unclasped hands due to widespread illiteracy, and a key group in this country, the National Islamic Front, was founded by Hassan al-Turabi.

question.leadin: According to an oft-repeated story, Robert Baden-Powell based the scouting salute on a gesture made by this empire's ruler Prempeh.
question.text: Name this empire with its capital at Kumasi. The final war between Britain and this empire began with Frederick Mitchell Hodgson's demand to sit on the Golden Stool.
question.clue: This empire was split off from the Denkyira Empire by its founder Osei Tutu.

swap.leadin: For much of the 20th century, this country claimed it was practicing a form of "separate development"
swap.text: Name this country which implemented the Pass Laws Act in 1952 to enforce restrictions on internal migration.
swap.clue: In that song, musicians pledged to not play at a casino resort in this country, "Sun City".

question.text: This ethnic group attempted to establish the Orange Free State and the Transvaal Republic. They descended from the early Dutch settlers who came to the Cape of Good Hope.
question.clue: Some argue that this African ethnic group's expansionist political aspirations originate with their ancestors' fervent Calvinism. The influence of the Freemasons is often compared to a "Brotherhood" of this ethnic group.

swap.leadin: A European trade war in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries here led to the unique geographies of some African nations.
swap.text: Name this country, formerly a British colony, located on a namesake river and with capital Banjul.
swap.clue: Operation Restore Democracy was a military intervention by ECOWAS in this country in January. It occurred because this country's President Yahya Jammeh refused to step down to make room for Adama Barrow. This country's capital is Banjul and it lies on either side of its namesake river.

question.text: As leader of the Mandingo people, Sundiata defeated this king of Kaniaga at Kirina.

swap.leadin: The capture of Dedan Kimathi symbolized the end of this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict in which the Kenya Land and Freedom Army rebelled against British colonialists.
swap.clue: Evelyn Baring declared a state of emergency in response to this revolt and helped oversee Operation Anvil, which forcibly relocated people from Nairobi.

question.text: Stanley led a relief expedition through "darkest Africa" in support of this governor of Equatoria, the successor of Charles Gordon. The expedition to relieve this man involved one of the first uses of the Maxim gun.

swap.leadin: The first President of this country had earlier been exiled due to his involvement with the Bwiti sect, which may have murdered young women after ritually consuming hallucinogenic iboga bark.
swap.text: Identify this African country where Leon M'ba was briefly ousted in a coup led by Jean-Hilaire Aubame before being restored by paratroopers sent by de Gaulle.
swap.clue: Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo.

question.text: In the 1830s, Sa'id moved his capital to this settlement to take advantage of lucrative local spice production. Tippu Tip ran a segment of the East African slave trade out of this settlement on the island of Zanzibar.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Leo Wolpert's favorite breakaway state, Katanga.
swap.text: When Patrice Lumumba became Congo's prime minister in 1960, this founder of the Belgian-backed CONAKAT party and president of Katanga declared the province's secession.
swap.clue: The main crisis of Lumumba's short time in office was the independence movement in the southern mineral-rich province of Katanga, which had Belgian backing. This man led that briefly-independent republic.

question.leadin: The atrocities of this regime were exposed by discoveries at their military compound at Kotebe. FTPE.
question.text: Name this Communist junta in power from 1974 to 1987 in Ethiopia, originally ruled by Tafari Benti. The famines caused by their radical land reforms were notably opposed by Bob Geldof.
question.clue: This regime originally consisted of approximately 120 soldiers under the rank of major.

swap.text: Mobutu called in Soviets in an attempt to stop this leader of the CONAKAT party from creating an independent nation out of the copper-rich province of Katanga.
swap.clue: Sharing of copper wealth and other issues led this Congolese politician to lead a Katangan secessionist movement in 1960, which in turn contributed to the downfall of Patrice Lumumba and led to a very strange relationship with Joseph Kasavubu.
